title: Risk-calibrated knowledge editing for large language models in robotic decision support
abstract: In robotic decision-support systems, large language models are increasingly used as knowledge and reasoning modules to interpret observations, retrieve procedures, and support action planning. For robots operating in long-running and dynamic environments, reliable decisions depend on factual knowledge that may evolve through updated procedures, new observations, corrected records, and expert feedback. Such systems therefore require the underlying language model to absorb new knowledge over time without full retraining. Sequential model editing provides an efficient way to update specific model knowledge, but repeated edits can accumulate interference and degrade previously edited or unrelated knowledge. Moreover, existing methods often apply nearly identical update rules to all edits, despite the fact that different edits may have different levels of reliability and conflict risk. We propose RACE, a risk-calibrated sequential editing method that assigns edit-specific update and preservation budgets. RACE builds a compact risk profile from target support, paraphrase stability, and historical proximity, and uses this profile to formulate a constrained memory update objective. The objective writes new knowledge while anchoring conflict-prone historical memories, yielding a closed-form update for efficient sequential editing. Experiments on two standard model editing benchmarks and two large language models show that RACE preserves competitive edit success while improving long-horizon stability, which is important for maintaining reliable knowledge modules in robotic decision support.

title: CogDrift-4D: Hierarchical Multimodal Modeling of Temporal Behavioral Decay for MCI Detection
abstract: Early detection of mild cognitive impairment remains a critical bottleneck in dementia care, demanding scalable tools capable of capturing subtle behavioral decay. To capture the subtle temporal changes of cognitive decline, we introduce a behavioral dataset collected across seven unscripted multimodal interactions over an 18-month horizon. This dataset formalizes continuous, multi-session interactions into a dense 4D tensor (Batch * Session * Time * Feature) that explicitly preserves concurrent local dynamics alongside long-term changes. To effectively process these complex behavioral patterns, we propose CogDrift-4D: a novel, hierarchical 4D Transformer framework. To capture the complex trajectory of cognitive decline, CogDrift-4D implements a dual-level behavioral fatigue and drift modeling architecture. At the intra-session level, the model computes localized least-squares regression slopes to quantify the acute ``fading'' of frame-level facial action units and acoustic energy. title: SAM3RL: Memory Control via Reinforcement Learning for Visual Object Tracking
abstract: Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) is a foundation model for image and video segmentation that sets the state of the art in visual object tracking. Its tracker, inherited from SAM 2, stores information from past frames in a memory bank, managed by a simple First-In-First-Out rule, allowing temporal consistency in complex videos. Several recent methods improve SAM 2 with hand-crafted memory update rules, each targeting a specific failure mode, such as distractors, occlusions, or object motion. However, their gains transfer only partially to the stronger SAM 3 backbone. We instead present a more general, data-driven approach that frames memory control as a sequential decision-making task. SAM3RL is an extension of the SAM 3 tracker with a lightweight memory controller, trained by reinforcement learning, that decides which frames enter the memory bank in order to maximize tracking performance. SAM3RL sets a new state of the art on 10 of 12 tracking and video object segmentation benchmarks, outperforming all hand-crafted rules without any runtime overhead. The same approach applied to SAM 2 gives SAM2RL, which outperforms hand-crafted rules on 9 of the 12 benchmarks, showing the generality of our method across model generations.

title: Quantum Folding in Chebyshev-Based Quantum Subspace Diagonalization
abstract: Quantum subspace diagonalization (QSD) with a Krylov space spanned by Chebyshev polynomials of the Hamiltonian is a natural ground-state method for fault-tolerant quantum computers, but every guarantee it offers---convergence rate, noise floor, and the cost of turning its classical output back into a physical state---is controlled by the overlap of the reference state with the true ground state, which decays exponentially with system size for any product state and non-trivial Hamiltonian. We propose quantum folding: for a system governed by a local Hamiltonian, seed the QSD with the product of the ground states of its subsystems, which differs from the target only through the interface terms. We prove a nonasymptotic error bound for the Chebyshev QSD that is linear in the measurement noise, by transplanting Kirby's effective-Hamiltonian analysis to the Chebyshev--Krylov basis, and identify the block-encoding rescaling of the Hamiltonian as a parameter of the guarantee. Exact simulations of antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains show that the folded reference state reduces the Krylov dimension for a given accuracy severalfold and lowers the error under noise by two to five orders of magnitude relative to the Néel state. We show how the Ritz vector is prepared as a physical state and that the ground-state generation probability obeys a tight ceiling set by the overlap, so that recursive folding prepares ground states at polynomial cost. Taken together, these results allow for a scalable QSD framework that avoids the exponentially small ground-state overlaps associated with conventional product-state initialization. Finally we compute the fold fidelity itself: a slow power law for the gapless spin-1/2 chain, a size-independent constant for the gapped spin-$1$ chain, and an exact closed form converging to 1/4 for the AKLT chain.

title: TVPara: Paralinguistic Captioning of Expressive TV-Series Speech in Complex Acoustic Environments
abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) struggle to parse paralinguistics (e.g., emotion, pace, pitch) in speech that combines intense emotion with complex acoustic environments. Strengthening this ability calls for training data that reflects such conditions. However, existing corpora rely heavily on studio-recorded speech, offering limited emotional and acoustic diversity. To address this gap, we introduce TVPara, a paralinguistic captioning dataset built from TV series. Speech in TV series often carries diverse emotional expression and co-occurs with scene-specific background sound, providing expressive emotion and complex acoustic environments at scale. Constructed via LALM pre-annotation and human correction, TVPara includes two tasks: Single-Utterance (~492h) and Multi-Utterance (~213h) Paralinguistic Captioning. Fine-tuning open-source LALMs on TVPara yields an average relative improvement of 31.26% in paralinguistic understanding under complex acoustic environments. The gains further generalize to an unseen TV series and to cleaner, cross-domain speech.

title: SKG: A Law-Induced Engine from Inference to Induction
abstract: This paper proposes the SKG (Symplectic-Kernel Gradient) reasoning engine for law-induced inference and induction. Laws are a priori; data provide instances. Inference is geometric evolution under law constraints. We organize symplectic geometry, GENERIC, kernel methods, RKHS, group-equivariant networks, and constrained mechanics into a unified, analyzable, implementable, verifiable framework. We propose the SKG octuple S = (M, g, omega, H, S, G, Delta, Pi), whose four components correspond to four levels of laws: conservation laws, constitutive relations, symmetry groups, and axiom systems. Main results: (1) Invariants enter metric construction via the Jacobian: g = J^T Sigma^-1 J + epsilon_G I. For constant cases, we establish inverse reconstruction theory: solvability rank condition (Thm 3.9), consistency criterion (Thm 3.11), and uniqueness theorem (Thm 3.14). (2) The kernel bandwidth matrix is uniquely determined by Fisher information and satisfies task-independence (Thm 3.19). (3) The metric reconstruction error decomposes into four terms (Thm 3.21), with squared condition number kappa(Sigma^*)^2 as the dominant amplification factor (Thm 3.22). (4) For state-dependent cases, we establish function-space reconstruction theory on matrix-valued RKHS (Thms 4.8, 4.9). (5) Three-layer projections handle axiom, symplectic-step, and conservation constraints. (6) The residual equation yields the observable formula, four-dimensional rank condition, and noise propagation, while g_qq is structurally unidentifiable. (7) Kernel parameterization yields the RKHS extrapolation bound (Thm 4.15) and strict OOD gain theorem in group directions (Thm 8.15). (8) The learning-decoupling theorem (Thm 9.1) proves the sole object of induction is the parameters of the task energy. Validation: 1D damped oscillator and 2D rotation-invariant system; 6 unit tests, 10 experiments (paired t-test, p < 0.01).

title: FUQAROLAR MUROJAATLARINI SEMANTIK TAHLIL QILISH VA VAQT QATORLARI ASOSIDA MUROJAATLAR OQIMINI PROGNOZLASH MODELLARI VA ALGORITMLARI
abstract: Mazkur maqolada davlat organlari, xususan, ichki ishlar organlariga fuqarolardan kelib tushayotgan ko'p sonli va turli formatdagi murojaatlarni intellektual qayta ishlash, ularning mazmunini tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash (NLP) usullari yordamida semantik tahlil qilish hamda dinamik vaqt qatorlari modellari asosida murojaatlar oqimini prognozlash masalalari tadqiq qilingan. An'anaviy usulda murojaatlarni qo'lda ro'yxatga olish va subyektiv tasniflashdagi kechikishlar tahlil qilinib, matnlarni morfolojik va semantik vektorlash (TF-IDF, so'z embeddinglari hamda transformer arxitekturalari), mavzuli klasterlash, sentiment (hissiy kayfiyat) va shoshilinchlik darajasini aniqlovchi ko'p bosqichli matematik model ishlab chiqildi. Murojaatlar oqimining mavsumiy va tasodifiy tebranishlarini hisobga oluvchi SARIMA (Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average) hamda chuqur rekurrent neyron tarmoqlar (LSTM — Long Short-Term Memory) integratsiyalashgan prognozlash algoritmi taklif etildi. Ishlab chiqilgan modellar va algoritmlar asosida «IIO-Analitika» axborot-tahliliy tizimining dasturiy prototipi yaratildi. Qashqadaryo viloyati ichki ishlar organlari misolida o'tkazilgan hisoblash eksperimentlari semantik tasniflash aniqligi F1-mezon bo'yicha 92.4% ga yetganligini, murojaatlar oqimini prognozlashda o'rtacha nisbiy xatolik (MAPE) 7.8% dan oshmaganligini hamda ijro intizomi va resurslarni taqsimlash samaradorligi 25–30% ga oshganligini ko'rsatdi.

title: Confidential Narrative Intelligence on a Local AI Box: Epistemic Symmetry Theory with Algebraic Mixture-of-Experts Routing
abstract: Financial institutions want to read the narrative of markets with language models, but much of what matters most — internal research, positions, committee notes, client communications — cannot leave their perimeter. This report describes how Epistemic Symmetry Theory (EST), a framework that detects regime changes in market narratives and explains what changed, is designed to run entirely on a local AI box. The system is organized as a Mixture-of-Experts in which the experts are local language models assigned to distinct offces (measuring, embedding, answering, generating, verifying) and to distinct domain hyperspaces, and in which routing is decided by deterministic algebra rather than by a learned gating network: a small, fast recognizer chooses; a capable model answers; every composition of operations is checked before it runs. We describe the architecture, the confidentiality model — what stays on the box, what may leave and only by the user’s choice — the EST engine that runs on top of it, hardware sizing, and the limits of the current evidence. The report is conceptual: proprietary implementation details are not disclosed.

title: Stylometry or Embeddings? Authorship Attribution for Russian and Italian Poetry
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) embeddings achieve strong performance in authorship attribution, yet it remains unclear which aspects of literary style they encode. We address this question through a residualization analysis of two poetry corpora: 5,800 Russian poems (29 authors) and 10,400 Italian poems spanning seven centuries (52 authors). Using a progressive residualization waterfall, we subtract interpretable stylometric features and high-dimensional lexical controls from embedding representations to quantify their contribution to attribution accuracy. For Russian poetry, residual signal collapses to near chance (1.1×) after accounting for character n-grams and word bigrams, indicating that embeddings largely compress orthographic and lexical distributions already exploited in classical stylometry. For Italian poetry, a reduced but significant residual persists (4.6× chance), consistent with diachronic or dialectal variation not fully captured by standard features. We conclude that embeddings and stylometry rely on overlapping signals but differ in how they weight lexical, semantic, and historical variation.

title: Probabilistic Anchor Graph Projection for Tensorized Unified Label Learning
abstract: Although anchor-graph-based multi-view clustering has achieved significant success in handling datasets with arbitrary shapes, current methods still face several challenges. First, many anchor-graph-based methods fail to fully exploit the structural information of the anchor graph. They directly apply regression or decomposition to the anchor graph, overlooking the similarity information between anchor points and data points, which leads to suboptimal clustering results. Second, many anchor-graph-based algorithms only consider sample labels, neglecting the impact of anchor point labels on sample labels. A further difficulty is that an imbalanced anchor distribution may not represent the sample distribution faithfully and can propagate biased assignments to the sample labels. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Probabilistic Anchor Graph Projection for Tensorized Unified Label Learning (PAGP-TULL) method. Specifically, we introduce a label propagation strategy into the regression process of the anchor graph, obtaining probabilistic projections of both anchor point labels and sample labels. Additionally, we stack the soft label matrices of all views into a third-order tensor and impose a tensor Schatten p-norm regularization to fully exploit the high-order complementary information and spatial low-rank structures embedded across different views. Furthermore, we introduce concept regression to reduce the number of variables and thus lower the algorithm’s complexity. We also fully exploit the structural information of the anchor graph, using anchor point labels to guide the learning of sample labels. At the same time, we design a novel balanced regularization term to prevent the occurrence of two trivial solutions for anchor point labels, thereby improving the robustness and performance of the method. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness and superiority of the PAGP-TULL method.

title: Structural control of two-level defect density revealed by high-throughput correlative measurements of Josephson junctions
abstract: Materials defects in Josephson junctions (JJs), often referred to as two-level systems (TLS), couple to superconducting qubits and are a critical bottleneck for scalable quantum processors. Despite their importance, understanding the microscopic sources of TLS and how to mitigate them has remained a major challenge. Here, we demonstrate a high-throughput, correlated approach to trace the microstructural origins of strongly-coupled TLS in Josephson circuits. We assembled a massive dataset of TLS across 6000 Al/AlOx/Al JJs and more than 600 atomic resolution transmission electron microscopy images. We statistically link fabrication, microstructure, and TLS occurrence, revealing a strong correlation between Al electrode thickness, Al grain size, and TLS density. Correspondingly, we find a two-thirds reduction in TLS prompted by a change in electrode fabrication parameters. These results demonstrate a robust, data-driven methodology to understand and control defects in quantum circuits and pave the way for significantly reducing TLS density.

title: A Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Multi-Stream Quickest Change Detection
abstract: A Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework is proposed for quickest change detection (QCD) where there are multiple experts, and each expert produces a sequence of statistics for change detection. A change is declared when a weighted sum of these statistics crosses a threshold. This framework is then applied to the problem of multi-stream QCD to obtain a family of powerful algorithms that outperform the best known algorithms in the literature. In the multi-stream QCD problem, a decision-maker observes multiple streams of observations. At the change point, the distribution of an unknown subset of the streams changes. The optimal algorithm based on a generalized likelihood ratio is computationally expensive. One of the most computationally and performance-efficient algorithms in the literature is the rank-weighted sum (RWS) scheme based on Shiryaev-Roberts statistics. It is shown in the paper that the MoE-based QCD algorithm for multi-stream data outperforms the RWS scheme. This is demonstrated through simulation results on real-valued Gaussian mean shift data and high-dimensional data from Gaussian--Bernoulli Restricted Boltzmann Machines (GB-RBMs).

title: ONCship: A Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Corpus for Ship Recognition
abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. Experiments on DeepShip and ShipsEar demonstrate the effectiveness of ONCship for acoustic representation learning, with joint pre-training on ONCship and AudioSet achieving a classification accuracy of 62.45% on DeepShip through linear probing. Furthermore, incorporating ONCship as auxiliary training data improves downstream vessel-type classification performance. Beyond conventional vessel-type classification, we further investigate MMSI-Level Vessel Classification, treating each vessel as a distinct identity. Experimental results show that models fine-tuned with different loss functions achieve Top-1 accuracies exceeding 53% and Top-5 accuracies approaching 69%, demonstrating the feasibility of distinguishing individual vessels through MMSI-Level Vessel Classification. Overall, ONCship provides a valuable resource for underwater acoustic representation learning and vessel recognition, while its rich vessel-level metadata enables further exploration of MMSI-Level Vessel Classification.

title: Revisiting Non-Adaptive Set Membership Schemes: Removing the Logarithmic Factor
abstract: We study non-adaptive bit-probe schemes for static set membership. Each query reads a fixed number of bits and answers by strict majority. We revisit the random bipartite-graph construction of Garg and Radhakrishnan [STACS, 2017]. The main observation is that a slightly stronger expansion property already bounds the number of exceptional elements. This makes a separate probabilistic estimate for exceptional elements unnecessary. A detailed union-bound calculation then gives, for every fixed $t\ge5$, a logarithm-free existence bound of $O_t(m^{1/c}n^{1-1/c})$, where $c=\lfloor(t-1)/2\rfloor$. For odd $t$, this removes the logarithmic factor from the general upper bound of Garg and Radhakrishnan [STACS, 2017].

title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
abstract: Spatial intelligence requires scalable 3D environments that are both photorealistic and semantically grounded, yet existing indoor datasets are dominated by room-scale captures and costly LiDAR acquisition. Online real-estate platforms offer abundant panoramas of diverse multi-room homes, but sparse viewpoints and texture-poor regions make reconstruction severely under-constrained. We introduce Holi-Spatial 360, a generative reconstruction and data curation framework for converting these panoramas into annotated multi-room 3D environments. Because reconstruction quality bounds subsequent generation, our Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization converts feed-forward reconstruction priors into reliable cross-view constraints and builds a coherent 3D Gaussian Splatting representation as 3D spatial memory. Adapted single-image and video priors then restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content. The reconstructed scenes support arbitrary RGB-D rendering and an automated curation pipeline that combines end-to-end 3D grounding with VLM-based verification. Holi360 contains over 1K multi-room 3DGS scenes, more than 100K instance annotations, and 2M spatial question-answer pairs. We also introduce the Holi360 benchmark to evaluate the spatial understanding of VLMs in real-world, multi-room indoor environments. Experiments demonstrate superior reconstruction and curation quality under sparse panoramic inputs, while fine-tuning VLMs on Holi360 substantially improves spatial reasoning capabilities.

title: KORXONALAR FAOLIYATIDA MIJOZLARGA XIZMAT KO‘RSATISHDA SUN’IY INTELLEKT (CHAT-BOTLAR)NING IQTISODIY SAMARADORLIGI
abstract: Ushbu maqolada raqamli iqtisodiyot sharoitida O‘zbekistondagi kichik va o‘rta biznes subyektlari faoliyatida sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarining, xususan, aqlli muloqot botlarining (chat-botlar) mijozlarga xizmat ko‘rsatishdagi iqtisodiy afzalliklari tahlil qilingan. Tadqiqotning asosiy maqsadi – kichik va o‘rta biznes korxonalarida an’anaviy inson mehnatiga asoslangan aloqa xizmatlaridan voz kechib, sun’iy intellekt botlarini joriy etishning moliyaviy rentabelligini miqdoriy jihatdan baholashdan iborat. Mavzuning dolzarbligi shundaki, an’anaviy aloqa markazlari (operatorlar faoliyati) hamda raqamli muloqot dasturlarining doimiy va o‘zgaruvchan xarajatlari o‘rtasidagi farq korxonalarda moliyaviy tejamkorlikni ta’minlashda hal qiluvchi ahamiyat kasb etmoqda. Tadqiqot metodologiyasi doirasida iqtisodiy-matematik modellashtirish, qiyosiy tahlil va kuzatuv usullaridan foydalanildi. Olingan asosiy natijalar shuni ko‘rsatadiki, raqamli usulga o‘tish korxonaning xizmat ko‘rsatish bilan bog‘liq xarajatlarini salkam 85 foizga qisqartiradi hamda xaridorlarning 70 foizi aynan algoritmik muloqotni afzal ko‘radi. Taklif etilayotgan yondashuvning ilmiy yangiligi shundan iboratki, sun’iy intellektning bevosita mikrodarajadagi (bitta mijozga xizmat ko‘rsatish tannarxi) iqtisodiy samaradorligi raqamlarda ifodalangan. Uning amaliy ahamiyati esa xizmat ko‘rsatish sohasiga aqlli texnologiyalarni integratsiya qilish bo‘yicha aniq xulosa va tavsiyalar ishlab chiqilganligida namoyon bo‘ladi.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Verification and Mutual Verification in Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate plausible but incorrect responses, and their ability to verify their own outputs is limited by uncertainty, shared reasoning biases, and insufficient access to independent evidence. Self-verification allows a model to inspect its own output, whereas mutual verification enables multiple models to evaluate one another's responses. However, relying exclusively on either mode may be inefficient or unreliable: self-verification can preserve the original model's errors, while mutual verification introduces additional computational costs and may propagate correlated mistakes. This paper proposes Adaptive Self–Mutual Verification (ASMV), a framework that dynamically switches between self-verification and mutual verification according to the estimated verification requirements of each generated response. The framework consists of an initial generation stage, a self-verification stage, a verification-state estimator, an adaptive mode-selection controller, a mutual-verification stage, and a final decision module. The controller considers uncertainty, disagreement, estimated error severity, verification history, evidence availability, and computational cost to determine whether a model should continue checking its own output or request verification from other models. Rather than treating self-verification and mutual verification as mutually exclusive system designs, ASMV treats them as complementary operational modes within a unified decision process. The paper formulates the framework mathematically, specifies an implementable algorithm, develops testable research hypotheses, and proposes an evaluation protocol covering reasoning accuracy, factuality, calibration, verification efficiency, and robustness. Because the framework has not yet been empirically evaluated in this paper, its expected benefits are presented as hypotheses rather than established results. The proposed research aims to investigate whether adaptive verification can provide a more effective balance between reliability, computational expenditure, and resistance to shared model errors than fixed verification strategies.

title: Requested Budgets, Realized Reasoning, and Answer Accuracy: An Empirical Audit of L1-Exact on MATH-500
abstract: Prompted token budgets provide a practical interface for allocating reasoning compute, but interpreting their effects requires specifying both the token boundary and the answer-scoring policy. We audit a pinned release of L1-Qwen-1.5B-Exact on all 500 MATH-500 problems at four requested budgets, with 16 seeded generations per problem and budget: 32,000 generations in total. Mean delimited reasoning lengths are 356, 865, 1,773, and 3,259 tokens for requests of 512, 1,024, 2,048, and 3,600; corresponding mean complete-output lengths are 400, 1,038, 2,040, and 3,537. The distinction is consistent with L1's complete-output training objective, and materially changes the measured adherence to the requested budget. Under the accepted evaluation workflow, answer accuracy is 69.16%, 77.04%, 80.24%, and 83.03%. The gain from the smallest to largest request is 13.86 percentage points, with a paired problem-bootstrap 95% interval of [11.60, 16.11]. The grading provenance is explicit: 31,567 deterministic comparisons, 405 AI judgments, and 28 single-reviewer human judgments. Twenty-seven accepted answers occur in unfinished reasoning outputs; requiring a closed reasoning boundary changes accuracy at the largest budget to 82.79%. We report this sensitivity, problem-difficulty heterogeneity, and immutable artifacts. Complete-output central 90% length intervals are disjoint across adjacent budgets, despite tail overlap in the observed ranges. The study is a checkpoint-specific measurement and replication audit, rather than a causal law of realized reasoning length or an independently human-validated accuracy benchmark. Code and analysis artifacts (v1.0.0): https://github.com/almohanna-ai/l1-budget-audit

title: A Cascaded-XCViT based Few-shot Classification Algorithm for Breast Ultrasound Images
abstract: Breast ultrasound serves as a cornerstone non-invasive technique for the screening and diagnosis of breast diseases. To address the challenge of limited feature generalization in few-shot learning for breast ultrasound image classification, this study proposes a novel cascaded Cross-Covariance Vision Transformer (XCViT) framework. A dual-stage architecture is introduced. Stage A employs hierarchical feature distillation via a three-level cascaded-XCViT module with Teacher–Student frameworks, generating dual-path tokens and utilizing token spectral clustering for semantic downsampling. Stage B uses frozen encoder outputs to derive prototype vectors from support-set features, enabling training-free inference via distance metric learning. Evaluation showed accuracies of 79.8% (1-shot) and 89.7% (5-shot) on CIFAR-FS, 47.2% (1-shot) and 67.3% (5-shot) on FC100, and 61.5% (5-shot) on a clinical breast ultrasound dataset, outperforming existing methods by 2.0–5.6%. The method demonstrates strong performance in low-data regimes and offers a promising solution for few-shot clinical auxiliary diagnosis.

title: RedDarwin: Evolving Jailbreak Skills against Frontier LLMs
abstract: Red teaming must continually adapt as frontier LLM safeguards evolve, yet existing approaches largely search for adversarial prompts or optimize within fixed attack procedures. We observe that even when an attack becomes ineffective, its underlying mechanisms can remain useful and can be revised or recombined to construct stronger attacks. Based on this insight, we introduce RedDarwin, an agentic framework that shifts the unit of jailbreak evolution from prompts and fixed attacks to executable attack skills. RedDarwin consists of 47 reusable base skills and autonomously revises, composes, executes, and selects them using target-model feedback, allowing successful discoveries to become building blocks for subsequent evolution. RedDarwin produces 65 evolved skills, improving 44 of 47 base attacks and increasing their mean attack success rate (ASR) on AdvBench from 18.8% to 47.3%. These evolved skills consistently outperform baselines on the held-out StrongREJECT and frontier LLMs unseen during evolution; with only 10 target-model queries, RedDarwin achieves 100% ASR on GPT-5.6-Sol, 92% on Claude-Sonnet-5, and 80% on Gemini-3.8-Flash. Analysis of the evolution trajectories further shows that strong attacks often emerge from novel combinations of reusable mechanisms rather than from individually dominant ones. We believe this paradigm can accelerate adaptive red teaming and inform stronger safeguards, creating complementary value for both safety evaluation and defense.

title: Machine-learning-based neutrino-event generation constrained by experimental measurements
abstract: We present a generative surrogate for charged-current \(ν_μ\)-nucleus scattering that can be calibrated to measured differential cross sections without event-level experimental samples. Starting from a theoretical interaction model, we fine-tune the surrogate to a MicroBooNE measurement and show that this also improves the description of observables not used in the fit. The calibrated model can also be applied to measurements from different neutrino fluxes without retuning, while retaining event-level predictions of outgoing-muon kinematics. Our results show that experimental cross sections can directly constrain generative event models while preserving their applicability across different observables and beam configurations.

title: Convergence Rates of Gaussian Process Thompson Sampling for Efficient Global Optimization
abstract: Efficient global optimization aims to identify a global optimum of an expensive black-box function within a limited evaluation budget $N$. We investigate the convergence rates of Gaussian process Thompson sampling (GP-TS) under noiseless observations, assuming a fixed objective function in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). For Matérn kernels with smoothness parameter $ν$ in dimension $d$, we establish a worst-case expected simple-regret upper bound of $O(N^{-ν/d}\sqrt{\log N})$ for both discrete GP-TS on sufficiently fine grids and its continuous counterpart. For the continuous implementation, we develop a nested-grid argument to control posterior sample paths over the entire domain. We further establish matching lower bounds of $Ω(N^{-5/2}\sqrt{\log N})$ for both implementations under a fixed one-dimensional Matérn-$5/2$ kernel, demonstrating that the logarithmic penalty is intrinsic to standard GP-TS in this setting. Motivated by this limitation, we propose Gaussian Process Capped Thompson Sampling (GP-CTS), which caps posterior sample paths using a valid RKHS norm upper bound while preserving optimism. This modification successfully eliminates the logarithmic penalty and achieves the minimax-optimal rate $Θ(N^{-ν/d})$ for both discrete and continuous implementations.

title: From complete channel order to capacity and one-way distillation
abstract: A universal construction that converts failure of complete quantum-channel information order into strictly positive ordinary private and quantum capacity. It claims an exact-zero capacity undecidability classification for finite rational-complex memoryless channels and corresponding positivity and zero classifications for one-way distillable entanglement and secret key. The state reductions retain any prescribed two-way distillation lower bound. The construction explicitly charges reference transmission and activation helper uses to the constructed channel. Strict positivity is distinguished from any uniform positive capacity gap; fixed-error capacity inapproximability is not claimed. The exact order-equivalence and undecidability premises are developed in the companion manuscript Complete information orders of quantum channels: equivalence and undecidability.

title: Text-to-Speech Bahasa Melayu Dialek Lubuk Kandis Menggunakan Metode VITS
abstract: The existence of numerous regional languages in Indonesia reflects the country's cultural richness, with their historical distribution forming various dialects. One of them is the Malay Language of the Lubuk Kandis Dialect. To support the preservation and dissemination of this language, this study applies speech synthesis technology in the form of Text-to-Speech (TTS) to generate speech output for the Lubuk Kandis dialect. A dataset consisting of 500 daily activity sentences was recorded by a native speaker of Lubuk Kandis and validated by a local linguistic expert. The Variational Inference with Adversarial Learning for End-to-End Text-to-Speech (VITS) method was adopted to produce speech output that resembles natural human voice. The evaluation used the Mean Opinion Score (MOS) test involving five respondents and resulted in an average score of 4.72, indicating that the generated speech falls into the good category. These findings demonstrate that the VITS method is effective in synthesizing natural and intelligible speech for the Malay Language of the Lubuk Kandis Dialect, providing potential support for the preservation of regional languages.

evidence.abstract: The existence of numerous regional languages in Indonesia reflects the country's cultural richness, with their historical distribution forming various dialects. One of them is the Malay Language of the Lubuk Kandis Dialect. To support the preservation and dissemination of this language, this study applies speech synthesis technology in the form of Text-to-Speech (TTS) to generate speech output for the Lubuk Kandis dialect. A dataset consisting of 500 daily activity sentences was recorded by a native speaker of Lubuk Kandis and validated by a local linguistic expert. The Variational Inference with Adversarial Learning for End-to-End Text-to-Speech (VITS) method was adopted to produce speech output that resembles natural human voice. The evaluation used the Mean Opinion Score (MOS) test involving five respondents and resulted in an average score of 4.72, indicating that the generated speech falls into the good category. These findings demonstrate that the VITS method is effective in synthesizing natural and intelligible speech for the Malay Language of the Lubuk Kandis Dialect, providing potential support for the preservation of regional languages.

title: A Lightweight Lattice-Based Post-Quantum Cryptographic Protocol for Secure Key Establishment in Resource-Constrained IoT Edge Devices
abstract: In this work, a lightweight post-quantum cryptographic protocol specifically designed for resource-constrained IoT edge devices is presented, addressing the vulnerability of conventional encryption to quantum computing attacks. The proposed protocol employs a modified NTRU-based algorithm with reduced parameter sizes, achieving switch production in 12.4 ms, encryption in 8.2 ms, and total energy consumption of 4.2 mJ per exchange - 63% lower than standard post-quantum protocols. Experimental results demonstrate resistance against quantum attacks exceeding 1018 processes while maintaining response times under 50 ms, with a compression mechanism reducing message size to 186 bytes. The protocol achieves an optimal balance between post-quantum security and operational efficiency, offering a practical solution for narrow-bandwidth, battery-limited IoT environments.

title: Dependent Dirichlet processes via thinning
abstract: We introduce a novel framework to model a collection of samples using dependent Dirichlet processes constructed through a thinning mechanism. The proposed approach modifies the stick-breaking representation of the Dirichlet process by thinning, that is, setting equal to zero a random subset of the beta random variables used in the original construction. This results in a collection of dependent random distributions that exhibit both shared and unique atoms, with the shared ones assigned distinct weights in each distribution. The generality of the construction allows expressing a wide variety of dependence structures among the elements of the generated random vectors. Moreover, its simplicity facilitates the characterization of several theoretical properties and the derivation of efficient computational methods for posterior inference. A simulation study illustrates how a modeling approach based on the proposed process reduces uncertainty in group-specific inferences while preventing excessive borrowing of information when the data indicate it is unnecessary. This added flexibility improves the accuracy of posterior inference, outperforming related state-of-the-art models. An application to the Collaborative Perinatal Project data highlights the model’s capability to estimate group-specific densities and uncover a meaningful partition of the observations, both within and across samples, providing valuable insights into the underlying data structure.

title: ARROWDE: an adaptive rotation-safe routed operator workflow for differential evolution
abstract: Optimizing continuous problems that combine rotated, non-separable, and multimodal landscapes under a limited budget of function evaluations is difficult. Most Differential Evolution (DE) methods use a static strategy or a fixed operator mixture, which can converge prematurely or spend the budget poorly when problem properties change during a run. This study proposes Adaptive Rotation-Safe Routed Operator Workflow Differential Evolution (ARROWDE). This bandit model combines upper-confidence-bound learning with landscape-aware priors, routing each trial to one of six single-evaluation operators: three exploratory and three exploitative. Implicit orthogonal transformations built from Givens rotations give robustness on rotated problems, and rotation-invariant population statistics are cached for the direct search operators at low cost. . On the CEC 2014 and CEC 2017 suites at 30 and 50 variables, ARROWDE attains the best mean Friedman ranks among the compared methods and is favored by the suite-level comparison against the most recent competition winner, with the margin widest at the higher dimension. The same tables mark its boundaries: IMODE and LSHADE-EpSin achieve lower mean errors on the 30-variable CEC 2014 composition functions, and the framework runs more slowly than L-SHADE and CMA-ES. Rather than proving every component strictly indispensable, ablation study ranks their relative importance, with stripping the rotation-safe layer causing the steepest performance drop, followed by the landscape prior and inherited adaptation, whereas the caps and bandit rule exhibit the smallest overall impact.

title: Deciphering Precambrian Litho-structural settings and barite-associated mineralization through integrated hyperspectral and geophysical datasets
abstract: Effective lithological mapping and mineral exploration remain challenging in geologically complex and underexplored Precambrian terrains. This is particularly relevant to the Arabian–Nubian Shield (ANS), a Neoproterozoic orogenic belt extending across northeastern Africa and Arabia. This study integrates Landsat 8/9, Sentinel-2, ASTER, PRecursore IperSpettrale della Missione Applicativa (PRISMA) hyperspectral imagery, gravity-derived structural analysis, supervised machine learning, and field observations to characterize lithology, alteration, and structural controls relevant to barite exploration in the Tehilla–Abu Samar area, Red Sea Hills, northeastern Sudan. Band ratios, principal component analysis, false-colour composites, Minimum Noise Fraction transformation, and Sequential Maximum Angle Convex Cone analysis were used to enhance lithological and mineral-sensitive spectral variations. Five classifiers—support vector machine (SVM), artificial neural network, random forest, k-nearest neighbors, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)—were evaluated for lithological classification. XGBoost achieved the highest overall accuracy (81.49%) and Kappa coefficient (0.792), closely followed by SVM (81.40%; κ = 0.791), while SVM yielded a marginally higher macro-F1 score. Gravity anomaly and edge-enhancement analyses delineated major NE–SW and NW–SE structural trends and density contrasts associated with intrusive bodies and deformation zones. Integration of independently derived lithological, spectral, structural, and field evidence established felsic metavolcanic rocks as the principal barite-hosting lithology and provided a coherent framework for prioritizing barite-associated geological targets in this structurally complex Precambrian terrane.

title: MolHop: Scaffold-Hopping Molecular Design with Agentic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Molecular design is often formulated as an optimization problem over existing molecular spaces. However, molecular optimization and the discovery of structurally distinct replacement molecules represent two fundamentally different search problems. LLM-based molecular design agents typically perform the former, conducting local refinement within the neighborhood of existing structures to improve target properties through structural modifications. In contrast, the latter requires exploration of a broader chemical space to discover molecules with entirely different scaffolds while preserving the functional characteristics of reference molecules. We propose MolHop, an agentic framework for cross-scaffold molecular discovery that enables models to navigate and edit within a pre-organized chemical space. MolHop organizes approximately 1.6 million molecular scaffolds from commercial molecules into a coarse-to-fine hierarchical action space. The agent selects new exploration regions through scaffold navigation actions and adjusts candidate properties through molecular editing. The framework maintains historical trajectory memory to support long-horizon search processes. On drug molecule and commercial compound tasks, connecting Grok-4.6 and DeepSeek-Flash-V4.1 to the MolHop framework substantially improves their cross-scaffold joint success rates. We develop MolHop-9B through agentic reinforcement learning, and MolHop-9B outperforms generative baselines including GPT-5.6-sol, Claude-5-Opus, and Gemini-3.1-Pro, while generating candidate molecules with larger scaffold differences from the reference molecules. These results demonstrate that effective molecular discovery beyond the traditional optimization paradigm requires structured chemical and action spaces, enabling agents to explore new structural regions rather than merely refine existing molecules.

title: Learning Individual Scientific Taste with Privileged Hindsight Distillation
abstract: Scientific taste shapes which research directions researchers pursue, and it varies across individuals. Existing work evaluates research directions along multiple evaluation criteria or models scientific taste using community feedback signals such as citations and reviews, but neither directly captures how individuals translate assessments under the same criteria into different preferences. We model scientific taste as a researcher-specific mapping from criterion-level assessments in a shared, evidence-grounded evaluation space with proposal-visible evidence, to relative preferences. A population-level mapping learned from retrospective supervision provides a cold start when individual feedback is scarce. We introduce Privileged Hindsight Distillation (PHD), which uses later-emerging scientific evidence during training to improve proposal-time criterion assessment and the population mapping, while exposing only proposal-visible information at inference. We evaluate our approach primarily in quantum research, where structured public reviews are largely unavailable, and use pairwise proposal comparison as a direct interface for observing individual taste. With only 15 comparisons per researcher, our method captures sharply different tastes, including opposing preferences over the same research-direction pairs when they trade off across evaluation criteria. In an interactive study, personalized rankings also surface proposals associated with greater subsequent user engagement, connecting learned taste to downstream research exploration.

title: Hamiltonian simulation for 3D elastic wave equations in homogeneous elastic media
abstract: We present an explicit quantum circuit construction for Hamiltonian simulation of a first-order velocity--stress formulation of the three-dimensional elastic wave equation in homogeneous isotropic media. Previous studies have shown how elastic wave equations can be cast into forms amenable to Hamiltonian simulation, but they typically rely on black box Hamiltonian access assumptions, making gate complexity estimation difficult. Starting from the first-order velocity--stress formulation, we discretize the system by finite differences, transform it into Schrödinger form, and exploit the separation between the component register and the spatial register to decompose the Hamiltonian into structured tensor product terms. This yields explicit implementations of first-order and second-order Trotter formulas for the resulting time evolution operator. We derive corresponding error bounds and constant sensitive qubit and CNOT complexity estimates in terms of the discretization parameter, simulation time, target accuracy, and material parameters. Numerical experiments validate the proposed framework through comparisons with the exact time evolution and reconstructed physical fields.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Independent Reasoning and Collaborative Reasoning for Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can perform reasoning independently, while multi-agent LLM systems can coordinate multiple reasoning processes to explore alternative solutions, exchange information, and resolve disagreements. However, independent reasoning and collaborative reasoning have different computational costs and potential benefits. Independent reasoning may be sufficient for straightforward problems, whereas collaborative reasoning may be beneficial when a problem involves substantial uncertainty, multiple competing hypotheses, or complex dependencies. Applying either mode uniformly may therefore lead to unnecessary computation or insufficient exploration. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Independent Reasoning and Collaborative Reasoning (AS-ICR), a conceptual framework in which multiple LLMs dynamically alternate between independent and collaborative reasoning according to the evolving state of a reasoning task. Unlike a fixed independent-reasoning pipeline or a permanently collaborative multi-agent architecture, AS-ICR treats the choice of reasoning mode as a sequential decision-making problem. Each model can independently develop and assess a reasoning trajectory. When predefined signals indicate that additional perspectives or cross-model information may be valuable, the system activates collaboration. Following information exchange, the system reassesses the reasoning state and may return to independent reasoning, continue collaboration, or terminate the process. The proposed framework incorporates uncertainty estimation, inter-model disagreement, progress assessment, task difficulty, and computational budget into a mode-selection mechanism. It also introduces explicit transition rules, a collaborative information exchange protocol, and an evaluation framework for examining reasoning accuracy, computational efficiency, robustness, and transition quality. This paper presents a methodological proposal rather than a claim of experimentally demonstrated improvement. Its central research question is whether adaptive, bidirectional switching can provide a more effective balance between reasoning quality and computational cost than fixed-mode alternatives.

title: Frozen LLM-Generated Preprocessing for Medical-Claims Adherence Classification: An Internal Model-Sensitivity Study
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate data-preprocessing code from data profiles, but their value relative to predefined expert workflows in clinical tabular classification remains unclear. This study evaluated whether frozen LLM-generated preprocessing matches a Manual Expert workflow for medication-adherence classification and identified the components responsible for performance differences. We analyzed 24,071 de-duplicated medical-claims records from 2022, comparing Manual Expert preprocessing against frozen code generated by DeepSeek, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, and iterative CAAFE. Stateful transformations were fitted exclusively within training folds. Performance was assessed using repeated 5 × 10-fold cross-validation, a locked 20% holdout with 2,000 bootstrap samples, and Nadeau–Bengio-corrected equivalence testing. With LightGBM, all pipelines were equivalent in accuracy, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Cross-validation accuracy ranged from 0.8204 to 0.8229, and every corrected 90% confidence interval remained within the prespecified ±0.01 equivalence margin; the widest interval extended from −0.0041 to 0.0009. Component ablation attributed the entire improvement over raw data to ratio features (+0.0018). Log1p transformations produced no improvement (+0.0000), whereas scaling slightly reduced accuracy (−0.0007), consistent with tree-based models’ insensitivity to monotonic transformations. Excluding the outcome-proximal variable UNITSTOTAL reduced holdout accuracy from 0.820 to 0.758 and AUC from 0.903 to 0.839, although pipeline equivalence persisted (accuracy span: 0.0018). However, equivalence depended on the estimator: naive Logistic Regression exhibited an accuracy span of 0.202, decreasing to 0.161 after uniform scaling and nested regularization tuning, with differences concentrated in CAAFE. Thus, frozen LLM-generated preprocessing can match expert-designed preprocessing for internal, tree-based medication-adherence classification. Gains primarily reflect feature construction rather than distributional adjustment. These findings also caution against assuming universal preprocessing superiority. Preprocessing strategies should therefore be evaluated jointly with downstream estimators, while claims-based prediction results require careful assessment of outcome-proximal information before being interpreted as genuine predictive performance.

title: Supporting data for "Efficient and Reliable Quantum Simulation"
abstract: Supporting numerical data and code for Chapters 3 and 4 of Wenjun Yu's PhD thesis, "Efficient and Reliable Quantum Simulation" (The University of Hong Kong, 2026). Chapter 3 contains Python code, notebooks, saved numerical data and figures for observable-driven Hamiltonian simulation. Chapter 4 contains MATLAB code and archived numerical results for Lindbladian simulation, together with figure reconstruction scripts and supplementary trajectory variance and standard-error estimates. The two repository snapshots preserve the exact commits cited in the thesis bibliography. The README provides repository attribution, file descriptions, software information and the limitations of the archived results; SHA256SUMS.txt provides archive checksums. Licensing: the Chapter 3 archive retains its original MIT license. CC BY-NC 4.0 applies to the Chapter 4 archive and the top-level documentation in this deposit; it does not replace or restrict the Chapter 3 MIT permissions.

title: How to enable fine-grained mobile network operator data analytics: The power of perturbative statistical disclosure control
abstract: Mobile network operator (MNO) data provide rich, high-resolution information that is valuable for a wide range of statistical analyses. In Germany, however, current data-privacy practices severely restrict the release of high-resolution datasets. This paper demonstrates that perturbative statistical disclosure control (SDC) methods can increase the utility of MNO data without compromising privacy by enabling the publication of higher-resolution aggregates under controlled noise mechanisms. After a brief overview of MNO data and the prevailing German privacy regulations, I introduce two tabular SDC techniques — the Cell-Key Method (CKM) and the Laplace Mechanism as an implementation of the Differential Privacy (DP) framework — and discuss their suitability for mobility data. I conduct an experimental evaluation using a dataset with device movements derived from real MNO records, generated at both low and high temporal resolutions. A systematic grid search over the space of the most important parameters of CKM and DP is performed, with the focus on utility rather than a full privacy-risk assessment. Results show that CKM delivers strong utility, especially for attribute combinations with low case counts, while DP either introduces unrealistic negative numbers or markedly inflates device movements. Compared with the traditional k-anonymity approach, perturbative SDC achieves comparable utility for k ≥ 5 and additionally permits the release of aggregates below this threshold, supporting finer-grained analyses. CKM also offers advantages in stakeholder communication and ease of implementation, although its integration into distributed computing environments remains an open research question. Overall, CKM emerges as a promising candidate for securely exporting high-resolution, aggregated MNO data to national statistical institutes, providing improved utility compared to the traditional k-anonymity approach while maintaining robust privacy protection.

title: Robustness of multivariate longitudinal finite mixture models to covariance misspecification
abstract: Multivariate longitudinal finite mixture models can identify subjects following similar developmental trajectories across multiple outcomes. Their use for this purpose is increasing, yet they are often analysed using software defaults or by restricting the covariance structure to aid model convergence. This study ascertains, through simulation, the effects of within-outcome variance-covariance misspecification under data conditions typically faced in practice. The performance of multivariate group-based trajectory models, latent class growth analysis, and covariance pattern growth mixture models is compared in terms of enumeration, classification, and class recovery. We show that restricted covariances, exacerbated by low class separation, can lead to poor class enumeration. Moreover, despite correctly specifying the number of classes a priori, variations in model performance across conditions emerge. An empirical data set is used to illustrate differences between the models in terms of enumeration and class recovery.

evidence.title: Robustness of multivariate longitudinal finite mixture models to covariance misspecification
evidence.abstract: Multivariate longitudinal finite mixture models can identify subjects following similar developmental trajectories across multiple outcomes. Their use for this purpose is increasing, yet they are often analysed using software defaults or by restricting the covariance structure to aid model convergence. This study ascertains, through simulation, the effects of within-outcome variance-covariance misspecification under data conditions typically faced in practice. The performance of multivariate group-based trajectory models, latent class growth analysis, and covariance pattern growth mixture models is compared in terms of enumeration, classification, and class recovery. We show that restricted covariances, exacerbated by low class separation, can lead to poor class enumeration. Moreover, despite correctly specifying the number of classes a priori, variations in model performance across conditions emerge. An empirical data set is used to illustrate differences between the models in terms of enumeration and class recovery.
evidence.venue: Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation

title: Lost in Translation: Why Lower Bias Scores Don't Mean Fairer Models
abstract: Bias audits of multilingual language models usually compare a model's average stereotype score in English with its average in another language and read the difference as a difference in fairness. We ask how much of that difference is noise. Auditing ten open models in eight languages, we measure how far scores move when English test items are merely reworded, test every language shift item by item, and check that the test catches shifts we inject on purpose. In all 70 model-language pairs the stereotype score falls below its English level, and for Hindi, Korean and Swahili the drop clearly exceeds what rewording English produces; most of it comes from StereoSet items. Judging every translation, we find that imperfect ones drop more, but faithful translations alone drop nearly as much. Still, a lower average does not show that a model is fairer. An item's English score predicts its translated score far less well than its reworded score (correlation 0.23, 0.27 on faithful translations, vs. 0.48), while scores stay as far from neutral, models agree on translated items, and within Hindi or Spanish a translated item's score correlates with its own rewording at 0.84 and 0.82. The average cannot distinguish lower bias from a different pattern of item-level scores. We also document three common pipeline errors that silently erase bias signal, and release our code.

title: Design Space Exploration of Reinforcement Learning Configurations for Post-Legalization Placement
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) have recently been explored for VLSI placement optimization, but their effectiveness for post-legalization placement refinement remains unclear. This paper presents a systematic design space exploration of a GNN-Proximal Policy Optimization (GNN-PPO) framework across three ISPD2015 benchmarks. We evaluate 18 configurations covering reward functions, GNN architectures, action spaces, candidate-set sizes, and training strategies. We analyse the results we obtain to identify pitfalls and to assess the prospects and opportunities of the RL methods for post-legalization placement. On top of that we propose a design classification approach to guide the design decisions of RL models.

title: Beyond DFT electronic band structures via dual-space orbital learning
abstract: Accurate electronic band structures are essential for predicting material properties, but high-fidelity calculations are computationally demanding. We introduce O-kRystal, a dual-space orbital-learning framework that uses a lower-cost Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) calculation as both an energy baseline and a source of structured orbital information. Combining PBE band energies with real- and reciprocal-space orbital matrices, O-kRystal predicts higher-level corrections for individual electronic states as a function of crystal momentum and spin. For states within 5 eV of the band-edge midpoint, it predicts Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof (HSE06) band energies with a mean absolute error of $0.171 \pm 0.009$ eV across nearly 6,000 three-dimensional materials spanning insulating, metallic, magnetic, and nonmagnetic systems. On a separate benchmark of six strongly correlated materials, it reduces the corresponding PBE band-energy MAE by 68.7% and resolves orbital-dependent changes in the relative placement of transition-metal d and ligand p states. Despite training only at high-symmetry points, it maintains comparable accuracy at unseen points along band paths and reconstructs HSE06 densities of states from dense Brillouin-zone predictions. Finally, training O-kRystal on $G_0W_0$ quasiparticle energies for two-dimensional materials demonstrates its applicability across levels of theory and the potential of orbital learning for higher-fidelity, momentum-resolved electronic-structure prediction beyond density functional theory.

title: Robota-Embed: Unified VLA Embeddings for Robot In-Context Learning and Evolution
abstract: Retrieving useful context for a robot requires matching its task, execution stage, and the continuation that should follow. We introduce Robota-Embed, to our knowledge the first vision-language-action (VLA) embedding model to jointly encode all three modalities in both current-state queries and recorded future continuations. Predictive retrieval training aligns these endpoints, enabling historical continuations to serve as context at inference time. We construct a multi-source corpus of 1,695,684 cleaned training anchors and introduce Robota-Embed-Bench, with 4,000 queries and a shared 8,000-entry gallery. Robota-Embed achieves 47.33% clip-level and 81.77% episode-level R@1, exceeding action-free Gemini Embedding 2 by 22.09 and 33.47 percentage points. Controlled retrieval studies show that removing native action degrades retrieval more than removing vision. We study two complementary applications. Embed2ICL uses retrieved experience for training-free and training-based policy conditioning, increasing success from 47.0% to 56.3% in DROID-Sim and from 86.4% to 92.8% on the LIBERO difficult subset, while improving task progress on real robots. Embed2Evolve uses execution feedback to grow task-local memory and refine context use around a frozen GPT-6 Astra policy. Across five ManiSkill tasks, it achieves 68% success, compared with 24% for GPT-6 Astra Direct and 33% for a harness independently evolved with Omni-Embed-Nemotron-3B under the same protocol. Relative to the latter, it uses approximately 79.5% fewer policy tokens per test rollout, counting both successes and failures. These results show that a unified, action-aware retrieval space can support robot in-context learning and task-local context evolution.

title: Smoothing out the edges: continuous-time estimation with Gaussian process motion priors on factor graphs
abstract: Continuous-time state estimation is gaining in popularity due to its abilities to provide smooth solutions, handle asynchronous sensors and interpolate between data points. While there are two main paradigms, parametric (e.g., temporal basis functions, splines) and nonparametric (Gaussian processes [GP]), the latter has seen less adoption despite its technical advantages and relative ease of implementation. This paper seeks to rectify this situation by providing a new simplified explanation of GP continuous-time estimation rooted in the language of factor graphs, which have become the de facto estimation paradigm in much of robotics. To simplify onboarding, this paper also provides three working examples implemented in the popular Georgia Tech Smoothing and Mapping estimation framework.

title: KO'P QATLAMLI MASHINA-EKSPERT TIZIMIDA QORAMOL KASALLIKLARI TASHXISLARINI MUVOFIQLASHTIRISHNING MATEMATIK MODELI
abstract: Ishda qoramol kasalliklarini aniqlashga mo‘ljallangan ko‘p qatlamlimashina-ekspert yondashuvida qoidalar bazasi, mashinali o‘rganish modeli, nazoratnamunalari, individual tarix va veterinariya bahosini o‘zaro muvofiqlashtirish masalasiko‘rib chiqiladi. Manbalar natijalari turli mazmunga ega ekanligi sababli ularnibirlashtirishdan oldin ma’lumotlarning yetarliligi, natijalar shkalasi va o‘zaro ziddiyatitekshirilishi zarur. Shu maqsadda uch qiymatli qoidaviy baho, manba mavjudligini hisobgaoluvchi vaznli umumlashtirish, ziddiyat ko‘rsatkichi va ekspert tekshiruviga o‘tishshartlaridan iborat tahliliy matematik model taklif etiladi. Model mavjud algoritmningtajribada tasdiqlangan nusxasi emas; u maqolada bayon etilgan jarayonni aniqlashtiruvchiva keyingi empirik tekshiruv uchun mo‘ljallangan yondashuvdir.

title: Dynamical Stability of an Operational Access Boundary Under Local Free Evolution
abstract: An earlier note derived, for two qubits coupled by a fixed controlled-NOT and an experimenterwith local capabilities on the target qubit only, that the accessible effects are exactly those of thealgebra A1 = M2 ⊗ span{I, Z}: a non-classical algebra is accessible while the control qubit’s phaseis not. That boundary was derived for a remainder with no dynamics of its own. This note askswhether it is maintained when the remainder evolves freely under a time-independent HamiltonianH = h1 X + h2 Y + h3 Z that is fixed and known, and the experimenter may insert waits ofany chosen duration, adaptively, anywhere in a protocol. The answer is an exact dichotomy. Theaccessible effect set, and its span, remain unchanged under every finite adaptive protocol if andonly if [H, Z] = 0, i.e. h1 = h2 = 0: the remainder may precess about the axis the interaction reads.For every other member of the family the failure is demonstrated operationally — an explicit pairof states that no protocol without waits can distinguish, and the existing readout protocol with asingle wait of duration π/(4|h|) whose acceptance probabilities differ by 1 − n3^4 > 0, n = h/|h|.For the control H = X the accessible span becomes all of M4, by thirteen named protocols; whetherevery effect of M4 is then implementable is left open. Invariance of a protocol’s statistics underchanges of its wait durations is defined and reported separately from preservation of the accessibleset; in this family the two coincide, for a reason that is stated. The closed form of the wait, thecommutation criterion and the span bound are standard material; the contribution is the worked,exactly-verified criterion at both the effect and the span level. Nothing about robustness or genericHamiltonians is claimed. Technical note, not peer-reviewed. The deposit contains the note and areproducibility archive (one exact-arithmetic script with 34 checks, a failure-path harness, the runrecord and a checksum manifest).

title: Verification package for "Verifying deployed bytecode against executable EVM semantics, with exact gas and no added axioms"
abstract: This package accompanies the paper "Verifying deployed bytecode against executable EVM semantics, with exact gas and no added axioms" (Seulkee Baek, 2026). It holds the records behind the paper's figures and tables, and the scripts that recompute them offline. The paper's statements refer to the Lean libraries Blanc, at commit 5048a51fb108d8d71dd58c897c4c62c8bff3b437 (archived by Software Heritage as swh:1:rev:5048a51fb108d8d71dd58c897c4c62c8bff3b437), and Jaune, at 2737c8ebcaec2f3a9a7014156403300bc664daab (swh:1:rev:2737c8ebcaec2f3a9a7014156403300bc664daab), with Lean v4.34.0. The proofs themselves live in those repositories; this package does not duplicate them. What it contains:- the on-chain records read for the paper at block 26,141,229 (7 October 2026) from three public RPC providers, including every WETH9 withdrawal and Uniswap V2 approve receipt compared in Sections 2.4 and 5.1 and Appendices C and D, the block-isolation records, the scripts that read them, and their outputs;- the commit-bound figures of the paper (library metrics, the generated-code share, the cost table, the claim map), each with the command that produced it, and `final-5048a51f/figures.md`, which maps every figure in the paper to its source;- the conformance-case inventory of the fixture release tests@v20.0.2;- `reproduce.py`, an offline entry point that, given clones of Blanc and Jaune, recomputes the commit-bound figures and the receipt comparisons from the shipped inputs and checks them against the recorded results; it needs Python 3.11 or newer and Git, no Python packages, no Lean and no network access. How to run it: git clone https://github.com/skbaek/blanc && git clone https://github.com/skbaek/jaunepython3 -I verification-package/reproduce.py --blanc blanc --jaune jaune \ --data verification-package --out NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY The output directory must not exist. On success the run prints one OK line, preceded by two SKIPPED lines for the third-party comparisons described below; any mismatch stops it with an error. The proofs are checked by building Blanc at the commit above (see the paper's Appendix E and Blanc's scripts/GATES.md), not by this script. What was left out, and why: copies of third-party documents (audit reports, papers, saved web pages, verified source files of others' contracts and the Uniswap npm build artifacts) are not redistributed here. THIRD_PARTY.md and third_party.json list each one with its original location and SHA-256, so a reader can fetch it and check it is the same file. Two of them, the @uniswap/v2-core build artifacts, feed two comparisons of reproduce.py (the npm factory runtime against the chain's bytes, and the npm pair runtime against the lifted bytes); without them the script reports those two comparisons as SKIPPED, and with them in place it runs them in full (`--require-third-party` makes their absence an error). The author's internal review notes and drafting history are also left out. Licences: scripts (.py, .sh, .swift) are under the MIT licence (LICENSE-MIT); all other files are under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-CC-BY-4.0), except ext/verity-ci-axiom-report-d42019149188/, a copy of Verity's own CI axiom report, which remains under Verity's MIT licence (see its PROVENANCE.md), and onchain/eips/eip-7002.txt and eip-7600.txt, text renderings of those EIPs, whose copyright is waived via CC0.

title: Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges
abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. This paper presents a structured narrative review supported by a systematic literature search of learning-enabled collaborative intelligence frameworks in SAR robotics, organized around three paradigms: human-to-machine (H2M), machine-to-machine (M2M), and machine-to-human (M2H) learning. The review examines recent developments in reinforcement learning, federated and decentralized learning, knowledge distillation, swarm intelligence, semantic communication, and the growing integration of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for knowledge grounding, transfer, and explainability. Beyond algorithmic advances, the analysis emphasizes deployment-oriented challenges including partial observability, communication constraints, uncertainty management, model reliability, and real-time operational requirements. Rather than conducting a fully PRISMA-compliant systematic review, this work synthesizes representative and influential studies to identify emerging trends, architectural trade-offs, deployment limitations, and future research directions for scalable and trustworthy collaborative SAR systems.

title: Semantic Wave Function Collapse: Natural-Language-Guided Constrained World Generation
abstract: Natural-language instructions can describe scenes through mandatory requirements, preferences, and contextual information. Conventional Wave Function Collapse (WFC) enforces local pattern compatibility but cannot, by itself, interpret these instructions or guarantee global requirements such as object counts and connectivity. We introduce Semantic-Constrained Probabilistic WFC (SC-PWFC), a compiler-generator-verifier framework that translates language into typed, executable scene specifications. SC-PWFC combines hard constraints, soft preferences, and contextual priors in an explicit probabilistic model. During scene construction, WFC-style propagation enforces local compatibility, global feasibility checks reject impossible partial scenes, and an independent verifier checks completed scenes. The framework also supports constrained completion, localized editing, and explicit handling of ambiguity and infeasibility. Controlled experiments demonstrate more accurate semantic compilation, more efficient constraint-aware generation, improved preference satisfaction and contextual consistency, and reliable preservation of protected content during editing. SC-PWFC thus extends WFC beyond local pattern generation towards language-guided, probabilistic, and verifiable scene synthesis.

evidence.title: Semantic Wave Function Collapse: Natural-Language-Guided Constrained World Generation
evidence.abstract: Natural-language instructions can describe scenes through mandatory requirements, preferences, and contextual information. Conventional Wave Function Collapse (WFC) enforces local pattern compatibility but cannot, by itself, interpret these instructions or guarantee global requirements such as object counts and connectivity. We introduce Semantic-Constrained Probabilistic WFC (SC-PWFC), a compiler-generator-verifier framework that translates language into typed, executable scene specifications. SC-PWFC combines hard constraints, soft preferences, and contextual priors in an explicit probabilistic model. During scene construction, WFC-style propagation enforces local compatibility, global feasibility checks reject impossible partial scenes, and an independent verifier checks completed scenes. The framework also supports constrained completion, localized editing, and explicit handling of ambiguity and infeasibility. Controlled experiments demonstrate more accurate semantic compilation, more efficient constraint-aware generation, improved preference satisfaction and contextual consistency, and reliable preservation of protected content during editing. SC-PWFC thus extends WFC beyond local pattern generation towards language-guided, probabilistic, and verifiable scene synthesis.

title: From Detection to Decision: Calibration and Deferral for Prompt-Injection Detection
abstract: Prompt-injection defenses are commonly evaluated as binary detectors, although deployed LLM applications must make operational decisions about whether to allow, block, or escalate potentially malicious inputs. Recent probabilistic decision models aim to support such decisions through calibrated confidence estimates, but their reliability under distribution shift remains uncertain. We evaluate a native probabilistic decision model (Jev), two Llama Prompt Guard 2 classifiers (22M and 86M), and an LLM-based judge on 47,611 held-out examples spanning direct and indirect prompt injections, hard-benign inputs, obfuscation, and distribution shift. Using separate development and calibration splits, we assess detection performance, probability calibration, and allow-block-defer policies under a frozen evaluation protocol. The LLM judge achieves the highest overall discrimination (AUROC 0.897), followed by Jev (0.871), Prompt Guard 2 86M (0.757), and Prompt Guard 2 22M (0.714). However, Jev's native probabilities do not consistently outperform post-hoc calibrated classifier scores, and temperature scaling improves calibration without improving discrimination. At an empirical false-negative-rate target of 1%, all evaluated gate-reviewer systems require more than 91.8% escalation and incur substantial false-positive rates. These findings demonstrate that probabilistic outputs alone do not establish reliable security decisions under distribution shift. Effective LLM security systems must jointly evaluate detection, calibration, reviewer behavior, and operational decision policies.

title: SHRED: Self-Play for Heterogeneous Road-Users without Expert Demonstrations
abstract: Realistic traffic simulation and autonomous planning both depend on modeling interactions among heterogeneous road users whose dynamics, constraints, and behaviors differ fundamentally. Existing approaches predominantly learn realistic interaction behavior from large-scale human driving demonstrations. In this work, we ask whether such behavior can instead emerge purely through self-play. We present SHRED, a framework that jointly trains vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists through large-scale heterogeneous self-play from random initialization, without demonstrations or logged-trajectory replay. SHRED combines type-specific dynamics and objectives with procedural scenario generation and per-agent randomization, allowing diverse behaviors to emerge through closed-loop interaction. On the Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge (WOSAC), SHRED jointly controls all three road-user types and outperforms both the closest demonstration-free self-play baseline and prior self-play methods that use demonstration-trained reference policies. Policies trained only on nuPlan map geometry retain comparable realism under zero-shot evaluation on Waymo. For planning, SHRED outperforms all compared planners on the interaction-heavy InterPlan benchmark. Controlled ablations show that heterogeneity in self-play improves both traffic realism and planning performance, with particularly large planning gains in interaction-heavy scenarios. Together, these results establish heterogeneous procedural self-play as a scalable, demonstration-free paradigm for learning realistic and interactive traffic behavior.
